route_notices.route: Data Download Program URLs (datadownload/Choose.aspx and datadownload/Output.aspx) and preformatted packages
route_notices.text: Q: Will the current DDP URLs (e.g., `datadownload/Choose.aspx?rel=...` or `datadownload/Output.aspx?rel=...&filetype=zip`) continue to work? A: No. These URLs will no longer be operational once the functionality is removed on March 31, 2027. To continue accessing release data on the Board's site, use the XML file linked from the release landing page (for example, https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/data/FRB_h41_xml.zip for the H.4.1).
route_notices.milestone: The registered route is the XML file linked from the H.6 landing page, which the Board says remains available. On the first due run on or after the date, confirm that the registered endpoint and releaseDates.json still answer in the registered format.

route_notices.text: Although the Data Download Program is being retired users continue to have access to expanded functionality through FRED ... The XML format is still available on Board statistical release pages for users who wish to manually download Board data from the Board's website.
route_notices.milestone: After the DDP page removal, confirm again that the registered endpoint and releaseDates.json still answer in the registered format.

nyfed-business-days.text: Published at about 9:00 a.m. ET on the business day after the rate's date; revised the same day only, except in extraordinary circumstances (New York Fed, checked 2026-11-16).

fiscaldata-release.text: Updated at the end of each business day with data from the previous business day (Fiscal Data, checked 2026-11-16). Calendar times such as 21:15 carry no stated time zone.

frb-h6-release-dates.text: Released on the fourth Tuesday of every month, generally at 1:00 p.m., with exceptions (Board, checked 2026-11-16); "For release at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time" (H.6 release of March 24, 2026, checked 2026-11-18).

known_inconsistencies.text: A Sunday record whose values equal those of Monday 2003-07-21; kept as published.

derived_from.method: Derived by RadMage Finance from the New York Fed's EFFR records: each change point is the first business day whose EFFR record shows a new target. Before December 16, 2008 the target was a single rate; from then on, a range.
